title: Jonah and the Veil
premise: Coral Halloran, a hedge-charmer sworn to the drowned god Veil, has hidden his gift for five years in Saltcross, a city where magic is outlawed and his god has gone silent. When the crown's witch-hunters begin burning anyone with the gift, Coral is exposed by a frightened apprentice he tried to protect, and flees with a ragged found family: a disgraced huntress, a child who hears the dead, and the very apprentice who betrayed him. Their flight becomes a pilgrimage to the drowned temple where the covenant between realms was first sworn, and Coral learns the Veil did not abandon its faithful—it was imprisoned by the crown's founders, who built their law on a stolen god. In the flooded dark beneath Saltcross, Coral must choose between restoring the covenant at the cost of his own name in the god's memory, or letting both realms go quiet forever; he gives up his name, reforges the covenant, and returns nameless but finally belonging, adopted by the family that refused to let him be forgotten.
about_author: I. M. Kavanagh is the pen name of a former tide-pool surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to fiction about gods that live in them. Kavanagh writes from a houseboat on an undisclosed estuary and claims all stories are just weather reports from other worlds.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral sells luck-knots and fever-wards in Saltcross's fish market, hiding his true gift beneath mundane craft while witch-hunters post new edicts on every corner. He tends a shrine to the silent Veil in secret, talking to a god that hasn't answered in five years. Emotional beat: weary tenderness—the ache of faith maintained alone.

chapters.title: The Edict of Ash
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The crown announces a census of 'afflicted' citizens; neighbors begin informing on one another for coin. Coral burns his mother's grimoire page by page, keeping only a single salt-stained leaf. A young apprentice, Wren, watches him do it and says nothing. Emotional beat: grief disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral takes Wren on as an apprentice in charm-making, teaching her only the safe, godless techniques. But Wren confesses she hears her dead brother singing in the harbor fog—a gift, not grief. Coral lies to her that it will fade. Emotional beat: protective denial beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Huntress Who Quit
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable Vane, once the crown's finest witch-hunter, drinks herself numb in a dockside tavern after refusing an order to burn a family. She recognizes Coral's charms as Veil-work when he patches a wounded smuggler. Instead of reporting him, she asks to buy one. Emotional beat: shame reaching toward redemption.

chapters.title: What the Fog Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren follows her brother's song into the harbor fog and finds the drowned temple's spire breaking the surface at low tide—evidence the old covenant site still exists. She tells Coral, who is terrified: if she found it, hunters can too. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Market
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Hunters raid the market following an anonymous tip. Coral shields Wren with open magic for the first time in five years, revealing himself to save her from a collapsing stall—and from a hunter's blade. They escape through the sewers with Sable's reluctant help. Emotional beat: sacrifice and the end of hiding.

chapters.title: Fugitives' Supper
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Hiding in a smuggler's cellar, the three share a stolen meal. Wren admits she was the informant—hunters threatened her grandmother. Coral cannot forgive her yet; Sable argues that family isn't earned clean. Emotional beat: anger, confession, and the fragile first stitch of found family.

chapters.title: The Silent God's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral deciphers the saved grimoire leaf: the Veil wasn't silent by choice. The crown's founders bound the god beneath the city, feeding on its covenant to power their law. Every outlawed spell was a prayer cut off mid-word. Emotional beat: revelation reframing five years of abandonment as theft.

chapters.title: Sable's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable reveals she helped bind the last free priests years ago, believing the crown's lie that magic caused the plague. Her hands shook ever since; the drink never fixed it. She offers Coral her knowledge of hunter routes and ritual protocols. Emotional beat: guilt transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: The Tide Road
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Guided by her brother's song, Wren leads them along the tidal flats toward the drowned temple at the ebb. Hunters pursue; Sable lays false trails using her old credentials. Wren realizes the dead aren't haunting her—they're guiding her. Emotional beat: fear becoming vocation.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Coral. They detour to rescue Wren's grandmother from the census wagons. The old woman refuses to leave her home but presses her wedding ring into Wren's hand—an heirloom of the pre-covenant faith. Coral sees Wren truly orphaned and chooses, silently, to stand in the gap. Emotional beat: inheritance passed under loss.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Weir
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Cornered at a river weir, the fugitives are recognized by Sable's former partner, Captain Ilex. Sable offers her surrender in exchange for the others' freedom; Ilex hesitates, then sounds the alarm anyway. They escape over the spillway, Sable wounded. Emotional beat: loyalty tested and bloodied.

chapters.title: Salt and Fever
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Sable's wound festers. While Coral works desperate Veil-magic to draw the infection out, Wren keeps vigil, singing her brother's song—and Sable, half-delirious, hums along, hearing her own dead for the first time. Emotional beat: tenderness in crisis; the group becomes a household.

chapters.title: The Drowned Spire
chapters.summary: POV Coral. At the lowest tide in a decade, they reach the temple spire and descend into airless halls kept dry by the bound god's last strength. Murals show the original covenant: not humans ruling magic, but humans and god sharing breath. Emotional beat: awe and homesickness for a faith never lived.

chapters.title: Prisoners of the Founders
chapters.summary: POV Coral. In the temple's heart they find the Veil: not dead but chained, its voice siphoned into the crown's law-stones. It recognizes Coral's oath and speaks his name—the first time in five years anyone has said it like it mattered. Emotional beat: reunion and heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Price of Breath
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Reforging the covenant requires a mortal anchor to hold the god's breath while the chains break—someone must give their name to the Veil, becoming remembered by no one. Sable volunteers, claiming her guilt as qualification. Coral refuses to let her carry it alone. Emotional beat: love arguing with sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ilex at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Captain Ilex and his hunters breach the temple, having tracked them across the flats. Wren steps between the blades and the altar and lets every ghost she's ever heard speak at once—the hunters hear their own dead asking why. Several lower their weapons; Ilex does not. Emotional beat: courage as witness.

chapters.title: Breaking the Chains
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Climax. Coral anchors the covenant as Sable and the defected hunters hold back Ilex. The chains shatter; the Veil's breath floods the temple, drowning the law-stones' power across the city. To hold the seal, Coral surrenders his name into the god's keeping. Emotional beat: transcendence through self-giving.

chapters.title: Nameless
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The flood recedes; the Veil is free, magic lawful again—but Coral stands blank-eyed, unable to recall himself. Wren refuses the price's finality: she sings his deeds back to him, the family's memory offered against the god's claim. The Veil, moved, returns his name as a gift rather than a wage. Emotional beat: fierce love outbargaining divinity.

chapters.title: A New Covenant
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Above ground, Saltcross wakes to working charms and falling edicts. Sable testifies before a provisional council about the founders' theft, accepting judgment for her past. Ilex, stripped of command, walks into exile rather than face what he defended. Emotional beat: accountability as the shape of peace.

chapters.title: The House on Tidewater Lane
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral reopens his charm stall openly, Wren apprenticing beside him, grandmother's ring on a cord around her neck. Sable fixes the leaking roof of their shared house. The Veil answers small prayers now—not grandly, just enough to feel heard. Emotional beat: ordinary joy as hard-won miracle.

chapters.title: What Belongs to Us
chapters.summary: POV Coral, closing frame. On the anniversary of the breaking, the four keep a supper for their dead—Wren's brother, Sable's burned families, Coral's mother. Coral writes his name in the ledger of the rebuilt temple, first entry in a book meant to be filled by many hands. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, inherited, and given forward.
